question.en: What type of bike is it?
question.de: Was für ein Fahrradtyp ist es?

help.en: A mountain bike has wide, knobbly tyres and a straight handlebar. A road or gravel bike has narrow tyres and often a curved handlebar. A trekking or city bike is made for everyday rides, often with mudguards, lights and a rack. A cargo bike carries loads in a box or on a long rack.
help.de: Ein Mountainbike hat breite, grobstollige Reifen und einen geraden Lenker. Ein Rennrad oder Gravelbike hat schmale Reifen und oft einen gebogenen Lenker. Ein Trekking- oder Stadtrad ist für den Alltag gemacht, oft mit Schutzblechen, Licht und Gepäckträger. Ein Lastenrad trägt Lasten in einer Kiste oder auf einem langen Gepäckträger.

help.en: An e-bike has a battery, usually on the frame or behind the seat post, and a motor at the pedals or in a wheel hub.
help.de: Ein E-Bike hat einen Akku, meist am Rahmen oder hinter der Sattelstütze, und einen Motor an den Pedalen oder in einer Radnabe.

question.en: Which gears does your bike have?

help.en: Look at the rear wheel. Chain and derailleur: several sprockets, and below them a part that guides the chain. Hub gear: one sprocket, and a thick hub in the middle of the wheel. Gearbox: one sprocket at the rear, and a box at the pedals. One gear only: one sprocket, and no shifter.
help.de: Schau dir das Hinterrad an. Kettenschaltung: mehrere Ritzel und darunter ein Teil, das die Kette führt. Nabenschaltung: ein Ritzel und eine dicke Nabe in der Mitte des Rads. Getriebe: hinten ein Ritzel und ein Kasten an den Pedalen. Nur ein Gang: ein Ritzel und kein Schalthebel.

facts.note: Only asked when drive.gear_type is derailleur, because conditions test it after the gear type.

question.en: How is your rear derailleur shifted?

help.en: Follow the shifter on the right of the handlebar to the rear derailleur. A thin cable in a housing means it shifts with a cable. A wire with a plug, or no wire at all, means it shifts electronically.
help.de: Folge dem Schalthebel rechts am Lenker bis zum Schaltwerk. Ein dünner Zug in einer Hülle heißt: Es schaltet mit einem Zug. Ein Kabel mit Stecker, oder gar kein Kabel, heißt: Es schaltet elektronisch.

facts.note: The heads of the limit and B screws. Never asked: it only picks the tool. Known from the bike's parts list or the derailleur model; when unknown, the tools screen shows both tools and how to tell them apart.

Where the rear gear cable's barrel adjuster is. Never asked as a question: the check barrel-adjuster-present (and its follow-up barrel-adjuster-search) sets it, and once known the check is not shown again. The 3D view draws the barrel there; inline is drawn at the shifter.

Detail fact, for example the name on the down tube. Entered in the garage.

riser.en: Riser bar, bent up at the ends
riser.de: Riser-Lenker, an den Enden nach oben gebogen

Bottom bracket drop: how far the bottom bracket sits below the wheel axles.

choices.question: How will you hold the bike while you work?

options.label: In a work stand
options.note: The easiest way. The rear wheel turns freely and the bike cannot fall.
options.warning: Heavy bikes, such as e-bikes, can be too heavy for a small stand. Check the stand's maximum load.

options.label: Hanging from a hook or a rope
options.note: The rear wheel hangs free, so you can turn the pedals by hand.
options.warning: The hook or rope must carry the whole bike. A heavy bike can fall and hurt you.

options.label: Upside down, on saddle and handlebar
options.note: Needs no tools. The rear wheel turns freely.
options.warning: Turning a heavy bike over can hurt you. Ask someone to help.

options.label: On its wheels, and test with short rides
options.note: Needs no tools, but takes longer. You adjust while the bike stands and test by riding.

states.description: The bike is clamped in a work stand.
states.put_back: Take the bike out of the stand.

states.description: The bike hangs from a hook or a rope.
The bike stands upside down on its saddle and handlebar.
states.put_back: Turn the bike back onto its wheels.

tools.name: Strong hook or rope that can carry the bike

substitutes.name: Bike multi-tool with a small cross-head bit
Bike multi-tool with small hex keys

tool_sets.name: A tool for the small screws on the rear derailleur
tool_sets.tell_apart: Look at the small screws on the back of the rear derailleur. A cross in the screw head needs the screwdriver. A six-sided hole needs a hex key.

inspections.title: Look at the rear derailleur
inspections.text: Stand behind the bike and look at the rear derailleur, the part below the sprockets that guides the chain.

animation.caption: A bent hanger tilts the derailleur

states.label: It hangs straight down, in line with the sprockets
states.meaning: The derailleur does not look bent.

states.label: It leans towards the spokes, or looks twisted
states.meaning: The derailleur or the part that holds it may be bent.

inspections.title: Find the barrel adjuster
inspections.text: Find the barrel adjuster: a small ribbed knob where the gear cable goes in. Look at the rear derailleur, then at the right shifter. If there is one at both, pick either.
inspections.question: Where is it?

states.label: At the derailleur
states.meaning: The cable tension can be set at the derailleur.

states.label: At the shifter
states.meaning: The cable tension can be set at the shifter. It works the same way.

inspections.title: Look along the cable
inspections.text: Follow the gear cable from the right shifter to the rear derailleur. On some bikes the barrel adjuster sits in the cable itself: a small ribbed knob, often near the handlebar.
inspections.question: Found it?

states.label: It is on the cable
states.meaning: The cable tension can be set there. It works the same way.

states.label: I still cannot find it
states.meaning: This bike may have no barrel adjuster.

inspections.title: Look at the chain
inspections.text: Look at the chain below the pedals. Turn the pedals backwards slowly to see all of it.

states.label: Clean, with a thin film of oil
Dry, rusty, or it squeaks
states.meaning: The chain needs cleaning and oil. If the gears still shift badly afterwards, check again.

states.label: Black and gritty
states.meaning: The chain needs cleaning and oil. If the gears still shift badly afterwards, check again.

inspections.title: Test ride the gears
inspections.text: Ride slowly on a quiet, flat path. Use only the right shifter and change one gear at a time, all the way up and down. Every gear should change quickly and run quietly.
inspections.question: Slow or rattling?

animation.caption: Shift one gear at a time while you ride

states.label: Slow or rattling when shifting to easier gears
states.meaning: The chain is slow to climb to the bigger sprockets, the easier gears.

states.label: Slow or rattling when shifting to harder gears
states.meaning: The chain is slow to drop to the smaller sprockets, the harder gears.

states.label: Every gear changes quickly and runs quietly

not_covered.text: Hub gears are not covered yet. They are adjusted differently from gears with a derailleur.
Gearboxes at the pedals are not covered yet.
Your bike has only one gear, so there are no gears to adjust. If the chain is loose, skips or clunks, a shop can help.
We need to know what kind of gears your bike has. Look at the rear wheel and come back.
Electronic shifting is not covered yet. It is adjusted with the maker's app or buttons, not with a cable.
We need to know whether your gears use a cable. Look at the right shifter and come back.

shop.tell: The rear gears shift slowly or noisily. Please adjust the rear derailleur and check the gear cable.
The chain is dry, dirty or rusty. Please clean and oil it, and check it for wear.
The rear gears do not work as they should. Please check the rear derailleur, the part that holds it, and the gear cable.

steps.title: Clamp the bike in the stand
steps.text: Clamp the seat post in the stand so the rear wheel hangs free. With a heavy bike, ask someone to help you lift it.

animation.caption: Close the clamp around the seat post

steps.title: Hang the bike up
steps.text: Hang the bike by the front of its saddle from a strong hook or rope, so the rear wheel is off the ground, and check that it hangs firmly before you let go. Never use thin string or a coat hook: it can break, and the bike falls.

animation.amount: until the rear wheel is off the ground
animation.caption: Lift the rear of the bike onto the hook

steps.title: Turn the bike over
steps.text: Lay a soft mat on the floor and turn the bike over onto its saddle and handlebar. With a heavy bike, ask someone to help.

animation.caption: Turn the bike over onto the mat

steps.title: Take the bike out of the stand
steps.text: Hold the bike, open the stand clamp and put the bike on its wheels. With a heavy bike, ask someone to help.

animation.caption: Open the clamp while you hold the bike

steps.title: Take the bike down
steps.text: Hold the bike, lift it off the hook or rope and put the rear wheel on the ground.

animation.amount: until the rear wheel is on the ground
animation.caption: Lift the bike off and set it down

steps.title: Turn the bike back over
steps.text: Turn the bike back onto its wheels. With a heavy bike, ask someone to help.

animation.caption: Turn the bike back onto its wheels

steps.title: Park the bike
steps.text: Put the bike on its kickstand, or lean it against a wall at the saddle and rear wheel, with the gears facing you. Never lean it on the handlebar: it can turn, and the bike falls.

steps.title: Shift to the hardest gear
steps.text: Turn the pedals forward by hand and use the right shifter until the chain sits on the smallest sprocket, the hardest gear.

steps.title: Shift to the easiest gear
steps.text: Turn the pedals slowly by hand and shift one gear at a time until the chain sits on the largest sprocket, the easiest gear. If the derailleur moves past it towards the spokes, stop turning the pedals at once.

animation.caption: Shift one gear at a time

steps.title: Set the cable tension
steps.text: Turn the pedals by hand and shift one gear at a time, through all gears and back. Watch the chain: every shift should be quick and quiet.
steps.question: Slow or noisy?

buttons.label: Slow or noisy shifting to easier gears
buttons.text: The cable is too loose. Look at the barrel adjuster from the side where the cable goes in, turn it counterclockwise a quarter turn, then shift again. Never turn it all the way out.

solution.caption: Turn the barrel adjuster counterclockwise a quarter turn

buttons.label: Slow or noisy shifting to harder gears
buttons.text: The cable is too tight. Look at the barrel adjuster from the side where the cable goes in, turn it clockwise a quarter turn, then shift again. If four turns do not help, a shop can check the cable.

solution.caption: Turn the barrel adjuster clockwise a quarter turn

steps.title: Test every gear
steps.text: Turn the pedals and shift through every gear, from the hardest to the easiest and back. Watch and listen: every gear should run quietly, and the chain should stay on the sprockets.
steps.question: Something wrong?

details.text: Your bike has {drive.rear_speeds} gears at the rear.

buttons.label: It rattles or jumps in some gears
buttons.text: Go back to the cable step and adjust as it says, then shift through again. If it does not get better, a shop can check the cable.

buttons.label: The chain falls off, or touches the spokes

exit.text: Do not ride: the chain can catch in the spokes and lock the wheel. Put the bike back on its wheels and take it to a shop.

steps.title: Ride into the hardest gear
steps.text: Ride slowly on a quiet path and shift into the hardest gear, the smallest sprocket. Listen to the chain, then stop and park the bike as before.

steps.title: Ride into the easiest gear
steps.text: Ride slowly and shift one gear at a time into the easiest gear, the largest sprocket, then stop and park the bike as before. If the chain moves past it towards the spokes, stop pedalling at once.

steps.title: Set the cable tension on short rides
steps.text: Ride slowly and shift one gear at a time, through all gears and back: every shift should be quick and quiet. Stop and park the bike before you turn anything.
steps.question: Slow or noisy?

buttons.label: Slow or noisy shifting to easier gears
buttons.text: The cable is too loose. Park the bike. Look at the barrel adjuster from the side where the cable goes in, turn it counterclockwise a quarter turn, then ride and shift again. Never turn it all the way out.

solution.caption: Turn the barrel adjuster counterclockwise a quarter turn

buttons.label: Slow or noisy shifting to harder gears
buttons.text: The cable is too tight. Park the bike. Look at the barrel adjuster from the side where the cable goes in, turn it clockwise a quarter turn, then ride and shift again. If four turns do not help, a shop can check the cable.

solution.caption: Turn the barrel adjuster clockwise a quarter turn

steps.title: Test every gear on a ride
steps.text: Ride once more and shift through every gear, from the hardest to the easiest and back. Watch and listen: every gear should run quietly, and the chain should stay on the sprockets.
steps.question: Something wrong?

details.text: Your bike has {drive.rear_speeds} gears at the rear.

buttons.label: It rattles or jumps in some gears
buttons.text: Park the bike, go back to the cable step and adjust as it says, then ride again. If it does not get better, a shop can check the cable.

buttons.label: The chain falls off, or touches the spokes

exit.text: Stop riding: the chain can catch in the spokes and lock the wheel. Push the bike to a shop.

steps.title: Set the outer limit (H screw)
steps.text: The chain is on the smallest sprocket. Look from directly behind the bike: the upper of the two small toothed wheels on the derailleur should be in line with the smallest sprocket.
steps.question: Not in line?

buttons.label: Further out, away from the spokes
buttons.text: The chain can fall off the outside and jam. With the screwdriver or hex key, turn the screw marked H clockwise a quarter turn at a time, until the toothed wheel is in line.

solution.caption: Turn the H screw clockwise a quarter turn

buttons.label: Further in, towards the spokes
buttons.text: The chain rattles or jumps to a bigger sprocket. With the screwdriver or hex key, turn the screw marked H counterclockwise a quarter turn at a time, until the toothed wheel is in line. If it does not move, stop turning: the cable holds it, and a later step sets the cable.

solution.caption: Turn the H screw counterclockwise a quarter turn

steps.title: Set the inner limit (L screw)
steps.text: The chain is on the largest sprocket. Look from directly behind the bike: the upper of the two small toothed wheels on the derailleur should be in line with the largest sprocket.
steps.question: Not in line?

buttons.label: Further in, towards the spokes
buttons.block: Do not ride like this: the chain can fall into the spokes. With the screwdriver or hex key, turn the screw marked L clockwise a quarter turn at a time, until the toothed wheel is in line.

solution.caption: Turn the L screw clockwise a quarter turn

buttons.label: Further out, away from the spokes
buttons.text: The chain rattles or slips off the largest sprocket. With the screwdriver or hex key, turn the screw marked L counterclockwise a quarter turn at a time, until the toothed wheel is in line.

solution.caption: Turn the L screw counterclockwise a quarter turn

steps.title: Double-check the inner limit
steps.text: Push the rear derailleur by hand towards the spokes, as far as it goes. Look from behind: the upper toothed wheel should stop in line with the largest sprocket.
steps.question: Does it go further in?

animation.caption: Push the derailleur in by hand

buttons.label: Past the largest sprocket, towards the spokes
buttons.block: Do not ride like this: the chain can fall into the spokes. With the screwdriver or hex key, turn the screw marked L clockwise a quarter turn, then push and look again.

solution.caption: Turn the L screw clockwise a quarter turn

steps.title: Check the gap to the sprockets
steps.text: Keep the chain on the largest sprocket. Look from the side: the gap between the upper toothed wheel of the derailleur and the sprocket should be small, and the teeth should not touch.
steps.question: Wrong gap?

details.text: The manual for {drive.rear_derailleur_model} gives the exact gap.

buttons.label: The wheel touches the sprocket, or almost
buttons.text: With the screwdriver or hex key, turn the B screw at the back of the derailleur clockwise, a little at a time, until there is a small gap.

solution.caption: Turn the B screw clockwise a little

buttons.label: A big gap, and shifting here was slow
buttons.text: With the screwdriver or hex key, turn the B screw counterclockwise, a little at a time, until the gap is small but the teeth do not touch.

solution.caption: Turn the B screw counterclockwise a little

exit.text: Do not ride. The derailleur or the part that holds it may be bent, and it can catch in the spokes. Take the bike to a shop.
Bikes without a barrel adjuster are not supported yet. A shop can set the gear cable for you.
Your gears still do not shift cleanly. You can ride carefully, but the cable may be worn or dirty. A shop can check it.
Your gears still do not shift cleanly. You can ride carefully, but the cable may be worn or dirty. A shop can check it.
